title: mini-batch lifecycle costspector and quant-hint advisor
author: Priya Menon
release_notes: Introduce a lightweight lifecycle-aware mini-batcher that tracks tenant warm/cold windows, a CLI for cost-sim dry-runs, and a quant-hint advisor that surfaces conservative quantization presets per workload.
description:
Context and motivation: Teams onboarded to Redwood often need fast, low-risk ways to compress end-to-end unit economics for bursty tenants without impacting latency SLOs. Existing autotuners operate post-facto; this change introduces a small "costspector" agent that observes mini-batch lifecycle signals (warm windows, idle decay, burst patterns) and synthesizes batch/caching defaults plus conservative per-tenant quantization hints so ops and SREs can dry-run effects before rollout.

Summary of changes: Adds a runtime-side lightweight lifecycle sampler, a deterministic simulator/CLI (costspector simulate) for running dry-runs on traces, and a quant-hint advisor that emits ranked presets (safe/medium/aggressive) with expected delta to token-cost and expected p95 latency impact. New modules: runtime/sampler, tools/costspector-cli, optimizer/quant-hint. No protocol changes; everything is opt-in behind feature flag "costspector.v1".

Checklist: [x] design doc (ENG-1973) linked; [x] unit + integration tests; [x] small e2e smoke in perf-canary; [x] feature-flag gated; [x] docs snippet in console-guides.

Commits (high-level): - 9a7f1f2: initial lifecycle sampler and persistence schema - b3e4c5d: simulator harness + dry-run CLI - f2d8aa0: quant-hint advisor and ranking model (heuristic) - a4b6c90: integration with tenant defaults and feature-flag gate - 0f1e2b3: tests, docs and perf-canary config

Files changed (overview): - runtime/sampler/* : new sampler that emits windowed signals and compact histograms - tools/costspector-cli/* : dry-run simulator, CSV/JSON trace importer, CLI flags for target SLO and budget - optimizer/quant_hint/* : heuristic advisor and preset exporter - console-guides/docs/snippets.md : short instructions and example outputs - tests/* : unit tests + synthetic trace fixtures - ci/perf-canary.yaml : added a smoke job to validate no regression on main perf metric

Design notes: The sampler is intentionally lightweight — it stores compact delta-encoded histograms keyed by tenant+model+shape and emits TTL'd summaries. The simulator replays summaries deterministically to estimate batching gains and cache hit curves. Quant-hint advisor currently uses a conservative heuristic (loss thresholds derived from historical evals in ENG-1973) and outputs three ranked presets with expected cost/latency deltas and a confidence score. This is meant to be advisory: operators must review and can run the CLI dry-run which outputs a side-by-side delta table.

Review conversation (selected): 
- Asha Rao (review): "Nice and focused; main concern is accidental promotion of aggressive quant presets for low-volume tenants. Can we limit aggressive presets to tenants with >1000 daily tokens or explicit opt-in?"
  - Author reply: "Agree. Added a guard in optimizer/quant_hint/policy.go: aggressive presets only returned when recent_24h_tokens >= 1000 or tenant opt-in flag set. Updated tests to cover this."
- Miguel Hernandez (review): "Sampler persistence format looks fine but validate on cluster upgrade path? Need a migration path for older persisted summaries."
  - Author reply: "Added migration snippet (runtime/sampler/migrations.go) and schema versioning. Migration is no-op unless feature flag toggled; documented fallback behavior in console-guides."
- Dana Kline (review): "CI flake on canary smoke; re-run and ensure timeouts are robust for slow runners."
  - Author reply: "Increased the canary job timeout and added a retry wrapper in ci/perf-canary.yaml. Verified green on re-run."

CI summary: All CI checks passed on the final push. Build: pass, Unit tests: pass (coverage +0.7%), Integration tests: pass, Lint: pass, Perf-canary: pass. One failing test on the first run (simulator edge-case with empty traces) was fixed by a guard in simulate.go.

Testing and validation: Local unit + integration tests, a perf-canary smoke job against a synthetic 10k-request trace, and a dry-run with a real tenant trace (anonymized) showed expected cost delta estimations within 8% of observed baseline. Conservatively the advisor defaults to safe presets for tenants below thresholds.

Backward compatibility and rollout: No API contract changes. Feature gated behind "costspector.v1". Migration is additive and idempotent. Rollout plan: enable feature flag for internal staging, run costspector simulate for top-20 tenants, review suggested presets in UI, enable in canary and then staggered rollout with monitoring of token-cost and p95 latency.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main. Commit message: "mini-batch lifecycle costspector + quant-hint advisor: sampler, simulator, CLI, quant heuristics (ENG-1973)". Post-merge actions: schedule a short runbook for SREs describing how to run the dry-run and evaluate presets; will follow up with a short Console guide and a blog blurb for the PLG spotlight.

Notes for follow-ups: - Improve advisor by plugging in small supervised model once we have labeled degradation pairs; tracked in ENG-2022. - Add exported CSV format for bulk evaluation and RBAC controls for who can push presets. - Consider integrating tenant warmstart signals with Dedicated autoscaler for joint warmup + batch sizing.
